P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: No. Under the Foreign Exchange and Foreign Trade Act, companies and individuals may freely conduct capital transactions and settlements with overseas parties, such as opening foreign deposit accounts. Since the 1998 amendment, prior approval and notification have in principle been abolished and replaced by after-the-fact reports for payments above a set amount, used for balance-of-payments statistics. The threshold is reported as JPY 30 million.

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: A sole proprietor (個人事業主) files a business-opening notification (開業届, kaigyō todoke) at the local tax office, generally within one month of starting. There is no registration fee and no commercial register entry. Filing the optional Blue Return application, generally within two months, unlocks a special deduction of up to ¥650,000, family-salary deductions and 3-year loss carry-forward. Foreigners need a status of residence that permits the activity (not researched).

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Residents (permanent residents, including all Japanese nationals) are taxed on worldwide income. Non-permanent residents are foreign nationals domiciled in Japan for five years or less out of the last ten. They are not taxed on foreign-source income unless it is paid in or remitted to Japan, but work performed in Japan is Japan-source. National income tax is progressive from 5% to 45% (45% from JPY 40m), plus a 2.1% reconstruction surtax on the national tax and roughly 10% local inhabitant's tax.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: Consumption tax is 10% (8% reduced). A sole proprietor becomes a taxable person if taxable sales in the base period (the year two years earlier) exceed JPY 10 million, or in the first half of the previous year (specified period). Export sales count toward the threshold. Voluntary registration is also possible, and is needed to issue qualified invoices under the invoice system from 1 October 2023. Exports and certain services to non-residents are zero-rated.

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law applicable to a small online business
L5_data_protection.answer: The Act on the Protection of Personal Information (APPI), enforced by the Personal Information Protection Commission, applies to any business, including sole traders and non-profits, that handles personal information of individuals in Japan, wherever located. It requires purpose notices, consent for sensitive data and for certain third-party and cross-border transfers. Corporate fines reach JPY 100 million.

L6_consumer_ecommerce.question: Consumer-protection / e-commerce rules for online sales (refunds, disclosures)
L6_consumer_ecommerce.answer: Under the Act on Specified Commercial Transactions (Art. 15-3), online and mail-order sales of goods can be cancelled within 8 days of delivery unless the seller's advertisement states its own return/cancellation terms. Online sellers must display the mandatory 'Tokushōhō' disclosures (seller identity, price, return terms and so on) and must not advertise misleadingly. There is no general cooling-off right for mail order beyond this.

L6_consumer_ecommerce.notes: Art. 15-3 covers goods and specified rights, not services. Waseda explainer cites the older article number (15-2).

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: none of the major platform barriers apply. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (5) Client payments by PayPal (on PayPal's Payouts list as 'Fully localized'). (6) Stripe accepts merchants here, so you can take card payments directly on your own site. (7) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
